classes.name: लोक सभा आम चुनाव
classes.name_en: House of the People (Lok Sabha) general elections
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Arts. 81 and 83(2): at most 530 members from the States and 20 from the Union territories, chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies, for five years from the first meeting unless sooner dissolved)
classes.note: First past the post in single-member parliamentary constituencies since 1962 (two- and three-member constituencies in 1951-52 and 1957), with seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes; 543 seats since 1977 under the 1976 and 2008 delimitations. The House can be dissolved early, so elections fell in 1977, 1980, 1984, 1989, 1991, 1996, 1998, and 1999 off a five-year rhythm. Two nominated Anglo-Indian seats ended in 2020.
classes.finest_note: The Commission's statistical reports give candidate votes by parliamentary constituency and by assembly segment; Form 20 polling-station returns are posted by each State's Chief Electoral Officer for recent elections.

cadence.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 83(2): "shall continue for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting and no longer"; Art. 324: the Election Commission conducts elections to Parliament)
cadence.vacancy_rule: A by-election within six months of the vacancy under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (class lok_sabha_by).

access.platform: Election Commission of India, Statistical Reports
access.evidence: Statistical reports for every general election since 1951-52 are listed on eci.gov.in, which answered HTTP 406 to the archive's User-Agent from this session on 2026-11-16 (results.eci.gov.in answered with a redirect and 404s for past result paths).

dates.note: Polling ran from October 1951 to February 1952; up to 1957 some constituencies returned two or three members (PIB footnote *), so the 489 seats sat in fewer constituencies.
Two-member constituencies still in use (PIB footnote *); they were abolished before 1962.

classes.name: लोक सभा उप-चुनाव
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 81; Art. 324)
classes.note: By-elections fill seats vacated by death, resignation, or disqualification, usually within six months under the Representation of the People Act, 1951; the Commission groups them into a few rounds a year with State by-elections.

access.platform: Election Commission of India, Statistical Reports
access.evidence: Bye-election results are filed under each year's statistical reports on eci.gov.in (HTTP 406 from this session).

dates.note: By-elections held in most years; not yet counted from an official list.

classes.name: राज्य सभा द्विवार्षिक चुनाव
classes.name_en: Council of States (Rajya Sabha) elections by State legislators
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 80(4): elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assembly of the State by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote; Art. 83(1): one third retire every second year; Fourth Schedule: 233 seats)
classes.note: 233 seats filled by State and Union territory assemblies by STV (open ballot since 2003), plus 12 members nominated by the President. One third retire every two years, so elections run in rounds through each year; many seats are filled unopposed.

access.platform: Election Commission of India, Statistical Reports
access.evidence: Results are issued as press notes by the Commission and the returning officers (eci.gov.in answered HTTP 406).

dates.note: Biennial and casual elections in most years; not yet counted.

classes.name: राष्ट्रपति निर्वाचन
classes.name_en: President, by an electoral college of MPs and MLAs
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Arts. 54 and 55: electoral college of the elected members of both Houses and of the State Legislative Assemblies (including Delhi and Puducherry), weighted votes, single transferable vote; Art. 56: five-year term; Art. 62)
classes.note: Weighted single transferable vote in an electoral college of about 4,800 MPs and MLAs; the 2022 election was the 16th (ECI/PN/56/2022). Votes are counted by State, so each State's ballot value is published.

cadence.locator: https://www.ceomanipur.nic.in/Documents/PressNote/presidential%20Election%202022/PN_56_09062022.pdf ("The term of office of Shri Ram Nath Kovind, President of India, is ending on 24th July, 2022 ... an election to fill the vacancy ... is required to be completed before the expiration of the term")
cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacancy by death, resignation, or removal is filled by an election within six months (Art. 62(2)), and the winner serves a full five years.

dates.note: Sixteen elections from 1952 to 2022 (ECI/PN/56/2022 calls 2022 the 16th); dates not yet listed from an official table.

classes.name: उपराष्ट्रपति निर्वाचन
classes.name_en: Vice-President, by the members of both Houses
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 66(1): elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament by the single transferable vote; Art. 67: five-year term)
classes.note: Members of both Houses, elected and nominated, vote by preferential ballot to a quota of half the valid votes plus one (Office of the Vice-President). Several early elections were unopposed. After the resignation of 21 July 2025 an early election was held on 9 September 2025, so the next term ends in 2030.

cadence.locator: https://vicepresidentofindia.nic.in/election-of-the-vice-president/ ("The election of the next Vice-President is to be held within 60 days of the expiry of the term of office of the outgoing Vice-President.")
cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacancy is filled by an election held as soon as possible (Art. 68(2)); the winner serves a full five years.

dates.note: Elections from 1952 to 2025, several unopposed; not yet listed from an official table.

classes.name: जनमत संग्रह
classes.name_en: Plebiscites and opinion polls under Union law
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Part XV (Arts. 324-329) provides for no referendum; the polls were held under special laws)
classes.note: The Constitution has no referendum. Two territorial votes were held by the Union: the Junagadh plebiscite of 20 February 1948 and the Goa, Daman and Diu opinion poll of 16 January 1967, which the Election Commission ran under the Goa, Daman and Diu (Opinion Poll) Act, 1966. Sikkim's 1975 referendum was held by Sikkim before it joined the Union and belongs to its own record.

classes.name: संविधान सभा
classes.name_en: Constituent Assembly, elected by the provincial assemblies (1946)
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india
classes.note: Members for the British Indian provinces were elected in July and August 1946 by the provincial legislative assemblies, by community, through the single transferable vote under the Cabinet Mission plan; the princely states' members were nominated. After Partition the Assembly sat as India's provisional Parliament until 1952.

classes.name: Central Legislative Assembly
classes.name_en: Central (Indian) Legislative Assembly of British India
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india
classes.note: Elected under the Government of India Act, 1919 in 1920, 1923, 1926, 1930, 1934, and 1945 by a property-qualified electorate in communal and general constituencies, alongside the Council of State. Its territory is shared with Pakistan, Bangladesh, and (to 1937) Myanmar.

classes.name: Provincial legislative councils and assemblies
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india
classes.note: Legislative councils elected in 1920, 1923, 1926, and 1930 under dyarchy, and legislative assemblies elected in 1937 and 1945-46 under the Government of India Act, 1935, in communal, general, and special constituencies. The provinces of 1946 became the Part A States of 1950.

classes.name: विधान सभा आम चुनाव
classes.name_en: State legislative assemblies (Vidhan Sabha) general elections
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Arts. 168, 170 (direct election from territorial constituencies, 60 to 500 members), and 172(1) (five years from the first meeting unless sooner dissolved))
classes.note: First past the post in single-member assembly constituencies (some two-member seats in 1951-52 and 1957), about 4,000 seats in all; each assembly keeps its own five-year term unless dissolved early or suspended under President's rule, so elections are staggered across the years and often share a polling season. Counted as one election per State; the 1951-52 and 1957 rounds also elected the assemblies of the Part A, B, and C States.
classes.finest_note: Candidate votes by assembly constituency in the Commission's statistical reports; Form 20 polling-station returns from each Chief Electoral Officer for recent elections.

cadence.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 172(1): "shall continue for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting and no longer"; Art. 324)
cadence.vacancy_rule: A by-election within six months (class vidhan_sabha_by).

access.platform: Election Commission of India, Statistical Reports
access.evidence: State assembly statistical reports for every general election since 1951-52 are listed on eci.gov.in (HTTP 406 from this session).

classes.name: विधान सभा उप-चुनाव
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Arts. 170 and 324)
classes.note: Held in rounds each year with Lok Sabha by-elections.

access.platform: Election Commission of India, Statistical Reports
access.evidence: Bye-election results under each year's statistical reports on eci.gov.in (HTTP 406 from this session).

dates.note: By-elections held in most years; not yet counted.

classes.name: विधान परिषद चुनाव
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 171(3)-(4): a third elected by local authorities, a twelfth by graduates, a twelfth by teachers, a third by the assembly, the rest nominated; STV in territorial constituencies)
classes.note: Six States have councils today (Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh); others were abolished or created under Art. 169 over time. Graduates' and teachers' constituencies are the only directly elected seats, with electorates of their own registered voters; local-authority and assembly seats are indirect. One third retire every two years.

access.platform: Election Commission of India, Statistical Reports
access.evidence: Council results are issued as press notes and returning-officer declarations (eci.gov.in HTTP 406 from this session).

dates.note: Biennial rounds in each State with a council; not yet counted.

classes.name: संघ राज्यक्षेत्र विधान सभा
classes.name_en: Union territory legislative assemblies (Delhi, Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir, and former UTs)
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 239A (legislatures for Union territories by Parliament's law) and Art. 239AA (Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies))
classes.note: Delhi elected an assembly as a Part C State in 1952, a Metropolitan Council from 1966, and an assembly again since 1993; Puducherry since 1964; Jammu and Kashmir as a Union territory since 2024 (as a State before 2019). Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, Goa, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh elected Union territory assemblies before statehood. Same rules and publisher as the State assemblies.

access.platform: Election Commission of India, Statistical Reports
access.evidence: Listed with the State assembly reports on eci.gov.in (HTTP 406 from this session).

dates.note: Delhi, Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir, and the former Union territory assemblies; not yet counted.

classes.name: Autonomous District Councils
classes.name_en: Autonomous district and regional councils of the Sixth Schedule
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Sixth Schedule para. 2(1): "a District Council for each autonomous district consisting of not more than thirty members, of whom not more than four persons shall be nominated by the Governor and the rest shall be elected on the basis of adult suffrage"; the Bodoland Territorial Council has 40 elected members)
classes.note: Ten councils in the tribal areas of Assam (Bodoland Territorial, Karbi Anglong, Dima Hasao), Meghalaya (Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills, Garo Hills), Tripura (Tripura Tribal Areas), and Mizoram (Chakma, Lai, Mara), elected for five years by first past the post and run by the State Election Commissions or the State governments.

classes.name: Statutory autonomous and hill councils
classes.name_en: Statutory autonomous councils outside the Sixth Schedule
classes.locator: https://lgdirectory.gov.in/welcome.do
classes.note: Councils created by State or Union law rather than the Sixth Schedule, among them the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils of Leh and Kargil, the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration in Darjeeling, and Assam's statutory councils (Rabha Hasong, Mising, Tiwa, and others), each elected by adult suffrage on its own schedule.

classes.name: ज़िला पंचायत सदस्य निर्वाचन
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 243C(2): all seats filled by persons chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies; Art. 243E: five years)
classes.note: Members elected by first past the post in territorial constituencies with reservations for women (a third or half, by State), SCs, and STs; most States hold all three tiers on one ballot day per district or State. Elections under State law also predate the 73rd Amendment (district boards from the 1880s, panchayati raj from 1959) and are not counted here.
classes.finest_note: Each State Election Commission publishes its own returns, one site and format per State (PDF result sheets, HTML portals, or gazette notifications); no national compilation exists. classes.note: Councillors (corporators) elected by first past the post in single-member wards. Corporations such as Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras elected councils long before 1992 under their own Acts; those elections are not yet counted. classes.name_en: Recall votes on municipal and panchayat heads
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 243R(2)(b) and 243C(5) leave the manner of choosing and removing chairpersons to State law)
classes.note: Some State laws let voters recall a directly elected municipal chairperson or sarpanch by a ballot of 'full chair, empty chair' (Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Bihar, and others), held by the State Election Commission on a petition of the councillors or voters.

classes.name_en: Chairpersons and mayors elected by council members
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 243C(5)(b): the chairperson of a panchayat at the intermediate or district level shall be elected by, and from amongst, the elected members thereof)
classes.disposition_reason: Votes of the elected members within each panchayat or council at its first meeting, like a speaker's election; the archive records the public elections that chose those members, not the internal choice of their heads.
classes.note: District and intermediate panchayat chairpersons by constitutional rule, and mayors and village heads in States that choose them indirectly.

classes.name: Traditional local bodies
classes.name_en: Traditional village councils outside Part IX
classes.locator: https://lgdirectory.gov.in/welcome.do
classes.disposition_reason: Part IX does not apply to Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and the Sixth Schedule areas (Art. 243M); their 14,163 traditional bodies (village councils, durbars, and headmen) are chosen by customary practice under State or district council law, not in elections run by an election commission.
classes.note: Counted by LGD as 14 district-level, 47 block-level, and 14,102 village-level traditional local bodies.

classes.name: सहकारी समिति निर्वाचन
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india
classes.disposition_reason: Boards elected by each society's own members under State cooperative laws (and the Cooperative Election Authority for multi-State societies); private membership electorates, not public elections.

classes.name: कृषि उपज मंडी समिति निर्वाचन
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india
classes.disposition_reason: Where State market laws still elect committee members, the electorates are licensed farmers, traders, and commission agents of each market yard, and many States now nominate the committees; limited-franchise bodies outside the public election system.

classes.name: Party candidate selection
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Part XV)
classes.disposition_reason: No law provides a state-run nominating contest; parties choose candidates internally and the Election Commission only receives nominations.

classes.name: न्यायाधीश
classes.locator: https://www.mea.gov.in/constitution-of-india (Art. 124(2) and Art. 217(1): judges are appointed by the President)
classes.disposition_reason: Judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts are appointed by the President (Arts. 124 and 217), and subordinate judges by the Governors; no judicial or law-enforcement office in India is elected.
